paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one entry per the pass instructions. The en field is identical to the zh field: every cell is a chemical symbol or a compound number, and the only German-language token on the page is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), which is left as printed so the header row matches the source. The table continues from the preceding page and continues onto the next: it opens mid-sequence at Nr. 179 with no Tabelle caption and no repeated caption row on this page, so the shared substituents fixed by that caption (and the drawn scaffold it belongs to) are not visible here and are not reproduced. The column heads are printed with superscripts, R with a raised 7a, 7b, 12 and 1; they are transcribed inline as R7a, R7b, R12, R1. Likewise the subscript digits in SO2, CH2, CH2CH2 and PhC(O)CH2 are printed as true subscripts and transcribed inline. The R12 cell of Nr. 193 is set one space further right than the PhSO2 entries above and below it; that is print alignment, not a different value, and the leading space is not carried into the transcription. The R1 column changes value inside the page: rows 179 to 197 read O-c-Pentyl and rows 198 to 205 read O-c-Bu. A short stray ink stroke sits in the R1 cell of Nr. 180, just above the O of O-c-Pentyl; a small dot sits in the R7a cell of Nr. 180 and another in the Nr. cell of Nr. 199; all three read as scan artifacts, not characters. The table body ends after Nr. 205 and the foot of the page below the table is blank.
